title: Fixed-sector global evolution descends to the proper classical quotient

reduced_flow.constraint_surface: Use K1373's closed neutral Gauss surface inside each fixed P_N phase space
reduced_flow.equivariance: The scalar-electrodynamics equations, Gauss constraint and conserved energy are equivariant under the admitted compact-circle gauge action
reduced_flow.global_representative_flow: K1397 supplies a global strong flow for smooth data and a global finite-energy flow on each fixed bounded-charge sector
reduced_flow.descent: Uniqueness and gauge equivariance identify gauge-related solution curves, so the representative flow descends to a single-valued global flow on the Coulomb quotient
reduced_flow.continuity: K1391 continuous dependence together with Coulomb projection and compact quotient topology gives a continuous reduced flow on every fixed sector
reduced_flow.positive_invariant: The nonnegative conserved classical energy is constant on gauge orbits and remains a coercive invariant on the reduced fixed-sector flow modulo harmonic connection motion
reduced_flow.cutoff_boundary: The family of reduced flows is defined for every finite N but no cutoff-uniform completed global reduced flow follows
reduced_flow.physical_boundary: A nonlinear classical reduced dynamical system is not a BV-BFV quantization or a positive nonzero GU physical Hilbert cohomology theorem
